sources.title: BirdLife South Africa, 2025 Red Data Book: African Fish Eagle

bird-african-fish-eagle.taxonomyNote: The checklist retains Haliaeetus vocifer. BirdLife South Africa lists Icthyophaga vocifer for IOC and Haliaeetus vocifer for BirdLife International; these refer to the same species in this account.

content.introduction: A waterside eagle whose adult white head contrasts with a brown body and dark wings.
identificationFeatures: Adults have a white head, breast and tail
Yellow bare face and feet; juveniles are browner
content.habitat: Rivers, lakes and reservoirs with suitable hunting perches; also some coastal waters.
content.behaviour: Hunts from perches, dives for fish and may steal prey from other waterbirds.
content.diet: Mainly fish, with birds and other small animals also taken.
content.groupStructure: Breeding pairs rear young; dispersing juveniles may gather together.
content.conservationStatus: Regional: Least Concern (BirdLife South Africa, 2025). Its 2024 global-status table also reports Least Concern, citing BirdLife International 2020.
interestingFacts: Rough structures on the feet help it grip slippery prey.

sources.title: BirdLife South Africa, 2025 Red Data Book: Saddle-billed Stork
sources.authors: Anonymous assessor; reviewers Andre Botha, Colleen Downs and Sanjo Rose

content.introduction: A tall black-and-white wetland stork with long legs and a striking multicoloured bill.
identificationFeatures: Adults have contrasting black-and-white plumage and a long colourful bill
Adult males have dark irises; females have yellow irises
content.habitat: Rivers, floodplains, wetlands and pans; nests and roosts in large trees.
content.behaviour: Stabs at aquatic prey in open water or flooded vegetation; generally resident, with local movements as water conditions change.
content.diet: Mostly fish, supplemented by amphibians, small reptiles and other aquatic animals.
content.groupStructure: Usually seen alone or in pairs.
content.conservationStatus: Regional: Endangered (BirdLife South Africa, 2025). Its 2024 global-status table reports Least Concern, citing BirdLife International 2016; regional and global categories differ.
interestingFacts: Kruger and adjacent areas form a core part of its South African range.
